Done — the two-week campaign ran Dec 18–31, 2026 and has now ended (line items were scheduled to stop at end of Dec 31 UK time). Here's the recap.

## Zero Shut Saturdays — New Year petition push: recap

**Setup:** One campaign ("Zero Shut Saturdays — New Year 2027 Petition Push"), two line items (~$16/day each, LINK_CLICKS goal, paid per link click, ALL_ON_TWITTER), targeting the UK only, age 18+ (AGE_OVER_18), as required by your own 18+ rule and X's political-campaigning rules (GB political campaigning pre-authorization was already on the account; both promoted posts came back approval_status ACCEPTED). No pixel on the site, so optimization and reporting are on link clicks; actual sign-ups are only visible on your side. Both approved posts were promoted head-to-head; I wrote no new copy and changed nothing mid-flight since performance was even.

**Totals (Dec 18 – Jan 1):**
- Spend: **$415.53** of the $450 budget
- Impressions: **430,548**
- Link clicks: **190** (~21.8% of… rather, ~$2.19 per link click)
- Billed engagements: 2,942

**By post:**
- Post 2132264302803165211 ("New Year's resolution: read more…") — $207.38 spent, 195,050 impressions, **98 link clicks**
- Post 2132445496737348185 ("£0. Thirty seconds…") — $208.15 spent, 235,498 impressions, **92 link clicks**

**Takeaways:** The two posts were statistically indistinguishable on clicks; the resolution-themed post was marginally more click-efficient per impression, the £0/30-seconds post got slightly more reach. Nothing disapproved, no delivery issues, pacing stayed under budget the whole fortnight. Since we can't see sign-ups from X's side, compare the 190 clicks against your own sign-up counts for Dec 18–31 to judge true conversion — and if one post clearly drove more sign-ups, that's the one to lead with next time (e.g., a spring push before the council pack presentations). One caveat to note: link clicks measure intent to visit the petition page, not completed signatures.
